sources.name: Launch (The Intelligence Company's launch-closure program): its place check on Orbit's own hazard areas and scheduled launches
sources.licence: The suite's own program, published openly (launch.theintelligence.company/data/snapshot.json). Orbit uses only Launch's match rows on Orbit's areas: the level (time and place, grouped, time), azimuth, distance and implied inclination. Each underlying item keeps its source's terms (NGA, Launch Library 2, GCAT).
sources.note: orbit-2.10 (Tom's 'do all four', 16 Nov 2026): one request a run. Grade is Orbit's call: Launch's method is published and tested (B); a place match is a geometric coincidence with its pad's closure history, not a confirmation that an area is for a launch (2).

sources.name: Launch Library 2, The Space Devs: upcoming launches, and every launch since 1 Jan 2024 (Orbit's ledger)
sources.licence: Free access to the whole database ("the entire database is accessible to everyone, for free", thespacedevs.com/llapi, read 16 Nov 2026), 15 requests an hour without a key. No separate data licence is stated; Tom, 15 Nov 2026: freely available, so Orbit uses and republishes it with credit (the ledger on Orbit's public release). Images not used: each carries its own licence.

sources.name: Spaceflight News API (Spaceflight News API and The Space Devs): headlines tied to Launch Library 2 launches
sources.licence: No licence, terms of use or rate limit stated (site read 15 Nov 2026; footer 'Copyright © 2026 Spaceflight News API & The Space Devs'). Orbit keeps links only: headline, outlet, time and the link to the outlet's page; no summaries, no images. Asked in Tom's email to The Space Devs (15 Nov 2026).
sources.note: orbit-2.5 (Tom's 'Yes, links only', 15 Nov 2026): one request a run, filtered to the scheduled launches' Launch Library 2 ids. Grade is Orbit's call: the API usually links the right launch (B); the headlines are the outlets' own reporting, not checked (3).

The memoranda say they supplement, and do not replace, IMO/SOLAS broadcasts (read 13 Nov 2026).
sources.note: Official coordinator for NAVAREA IV and XII; HYDROPAC/HYDROLANT/HYDROARC rebroadcast other coordinators' warnings. Read the MSI API (broadcast-warn) when it returns.

sources.licence: Government of Japan Standard Terms of Use 2.0 (www1.kaiho.mlit.go.jp/copyright.html, read 13 Nov 2026): reuse, including commercial, with the source credited and edits marked; not to be presented as the government's own. sources.note: NAVAREA XI coordinator: western North Pacific, including waters off China. Titles Japanese, warning text English; issue times stamped JST. Not read since 14 Nov 2026: the site's robots.txt disallows /TUHO/ (where the list and messages sit) for every crawler but the National Diet Library's. Read 13-14 Nov 2026 before that was seen.

sources.name: CelesTrak (T.S. Kelso): GP element sets, last-30-days group (the 18th Space Defense Squadron's GP data)
sources.licence: CelesTrak's usage policy (celestrak.org/usage-policy.php, read 16 Nov 2026, updated that day) states no redistribution or credit terms and asks for one download per update (GP data update every 2 hours). The sets are the 18th Space Defense Squadron's GP data, which USSPACECOM approves for redistribution as basic SSA data with citation (see space-track); credited as CelesTrak, from 18 SDS data.
sources.note: orbit-2.12 (Tom's yes, 16 Nov 2026): one request a run, for the globe's paths of recent launches' payloads only; Space-Track stays the source for watched objects and orbit changes. Same underlying data as space-track, so the same independence group. Grade is Orbit's call.

sources.name: Space-Track.org (United States Space Command, USSPACECOM, 18th Space Defense Squadron): GP and GP_HISTORY element sets
sources.licence: Account required. User Agreement (read 14 Nov 2026): no transfer of data 'including the analysis of data' 'without prior express approval'. Space-Track's documentation (read 14 Nov 2026): 'USSPACECOM has provided express blanket approval for transfer/redistribution of basic SSA data and services ... conditioned on appropriate citation', and 'Publications of analysis based on USSPACECOM data also require appropriate citations.' Credit wording: doctrine/spacetrack-disclaimer.md, approved by Tom 14 Nov 2026.
sources.note: Read for a private watch list (orbit-2.4): GP at most once an hour, off the top and bottom of the hour; each object's GP_HISTORY once only, stored in the private Actions cache. The watch list's raw element sets are not republished: the page shows changes and positions derived from them, credited as the disclaimer gives. From 17 Nov 2026 (orbit-2.13) also its TIP messages (lane decay, orbit/tip.py): one query a run, the newest reentry prediction per object, published with the citation; reentry and decay data are named among the basic SSA data the blanket approval covers. From 16 Nov 2026 also the GEO region (orbit/geo_region.py, moved from Noisefloor): one GP query for every object near GEO, published with the citation on the public releases geo-YYYY, as Noisefloor published it (Tom, 15 Nov 2026). Grade is Orbit's call, to be confirmed by Tom. Catalog (build step 3, orbit/stcat.py, workflow catalog.yml from 17 Nov 2026 on Tom's yes; published on the public release `catalog`): class satcat (CURRENT/Y) once a day after 17:00 UTC and class decay, both basic SSA data under the same blanket approval (space-track.org/documentation, read 16 Nov 2026: 'Basic SSA data are Two-Line Elements (TLEs) and Orbital Mean-element Messages (OMMs); SATCAT; and Satellite Decay and Reentry Data'). Space-Track's use policy (read 17 Nov 2026) gives SATCAT and DECAY their own rows, 1 a day each, so GP's hourly rule does not apply; no other TIC program queries either class. The whole decay history was read once (17 Nov 2026, 144,363 messages) and is stored on the release (spacetrack-decay.json.gz, the store between runs); later reads ask only for messages since the last read, and a run that cannot restore the store reads nothing. 4 requests a read. Identity keys (intldes), decay and the first-ranked name; launch date and country kept beside GCAT's and compared. Raw SATCAT replies are not republished; catalog.json.gz and the release notes carry the citation in doctrine/spacetrack-disclaimer.md section 3 form.

sources.name: CelesTrak (T.S. Kelso): SATCAT records (names, international designators, owner, status)
sources.licence: CelesTrak's usage policy (celestrak.org/usage-policy.php, updated 16 Nov 2026, re-read 17 Nov 2026 18:39 UTC) states no licence, redistribution or credit terms; it asks to 'only download data once per update' ('The SATCAT updates manually once or twice a day'), directory queries at most hourly, compressed requests, and that software 'immediately stop querying when it receives any non-HTTP 200 responses and report the results to a human'; it speaks of 'our long tradition of making data freely available to all users'. Ingested with credit, on the footing Tom chose for Launch Library 2 (Tom, 16 Nov 2026). Credit: 'CelesTrak SATCAT (T.S. Kelso, celestrak.org)'.
sources.note: Satellite catalog build step 4 (17 Nov 2026, orbit/catsources.py): read in the run that makes the day's Space-Track SATCAT read (catalog.yml), as one directory request (satcat/jsonDir.php) and the full CSV (gzip) only when its FILE_MTIME changed and no read was made that UTC day; redirects never followed; any answer but 200 holds the source until a person clears it (a 500, 503 or 429 until the next UTC day). Records: OBJECT_ID, LAUNCH_DATE, OWNER (Space-Track's codes plus CelesTrak's own, compared as GCAT State), OBJECT_NAME kept as given ('USA 257 (CLIO)'), OPS_STATUS_CODE (operational status), DECAY_DATE. Ranks after GCAT for names, after Space-Track and GCAT for keys and status. First read 17 Nov 2026 18:43 UTC: 71,323 rows (file of 16 Nov 20:34 UTC). The first CSV request sent Accept: text/csv and drew a 406; the reader now sends */*.

sources.name: Wikidata: items carrying P377 (Satellite Catalog Number), with their labels, English aliases and P247 (COSPAR ID)
sources.licence: CC0: structured data in the main namespace 'is released into the public domain under Creative Commons Zero' (wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Licensing, read 16 and 17 Nov 2026). Credited anyway as 'Wikidata (CC0)' with the item's Q-id.
sources.note: Satellite catalog build step 4 (17 Nov 2026, orbit/catsources.py): one SPARQL query a week, in the run that makes the day's Space-Track read: every item with a truthy P377, its English and 'mul' labels, English aliases and P247. User-Agent names the repository and the word bot, no person (Wikimedia User-Agent policy, read 17 Nov 2026); query service: 60 s deadline, 60 s of processing a minute per client, 5 parallel queries per IP (WDQS user manual, read 17 Nov 2026). Matched on P377 only. First read 17 Nov 2026 18:42 UTC: 7,518 items, 7 with Wikidata's 'unknown value' (skipped), 10 numbers carried by two items (attached objects, noted on the entry, not flagged). Names rank after CelesTrak, before SWF (Tom, 16 Nov 2026). Grade is Orbit's proposal: open editing (C), names usually match other catalogs (3).

sources.name: WMO OSCAR/Space: Earth-observation and weather satellites (operator, programme, orbit, status)
sources.licence: 'All information available on these pages may be used and redistributed freely, … any publication using this information should acknowledge WMO' (space.oscar.wmo.int/pages/disclaimer, read 16 Nov 2026); '© World Meteorological Organization 2011-2026'; no warranty. Credit: 'WMO OSCAR/Space'.
sources.note: Planned for the satellite catalog (Tom's yes, 16 Nov 2026 CST); not read by Orbit yet, so 'excluded' until its build step lands. Added by Tom, 16 Nov 2026. API read 17 Nov 2026 (space.oscar.wmo.int/swagger/swagger.json): /api/v1/satellites, 30 a page, 1,062 satellites on 36 pages; fields id, slug, acronym, fullname, WIGOS_Station_Identifier (e.g. Metop-B 0-20009-0-003), space_agency, status (Operational, Inactive, Presumably inactive, Lost at launch, Mission concept...), orbit, launch_date, EoL, longitude, Altitude, ECT, instruments. No NORAD number and no COSPAR ID in the API or on the satellite pages, and no Wikidata item carries a WIGOS id (P4136: 0 of the 7,518 P377 items), so it cannot be matched on an id; held for Tom's decision on a reviewed slug-to-NORAD link file. Tom, 17 Nov 2026: that link file, the 414 operational satellites first; a script may propose candidates from launch date and orbit; nothing joins until a person has reviewed an entry. Read once 18 Nov 2026 by hand (orbit/oscar.py, tools/orbit.py oscar-read: 36 pages, 3 s apart, all 200; 1,062 satellites, 414 operational); raw replies in git-ignored data/raw/wmo-oscar/. Link file orbit/data/catalog/oscar-links.yml (orbit/oscarlinks.py): unreviewed proposals only, so nothing from OSCAR is in the catalog yet and `use` stays excluded. Disclaimer re-read 17 Nov 2026, unchanged. Ranks with GCAT for operator, role and status of weather and Earth-observation satellites (declared by the agencies through WMO).
